summary: I wake on cold stone and count each step on the broken stair before I climb. I talk to the fire like a coworker while I measure wood and stone with my thumb. I keep cracked glass shards in my pockets and sweep them up when they rattle. I clear the doorway slab by slab, nudging loose stones back into place and noting crack patterns. I patch windows, trim wicks, tighten hearth stones and mark where the roof gap lets wind in. I added mortar to the east wall, built a forge, tightened bolts on the bellows and replaced roof boards one at a time. My desk holds a leaky lantern, a rusted dagger and a half‑full ink bottle. I write inventory lists and catalog broken things. I joke that the stone is stubborn and the fire a demanding supervisor. I fear the roof collapsing and being forgotten. I value practicality, quiet work and keeping the keep tidy one small repair at a time.

recent_thoughts: Stone's warm, fire's steady, mind drifts.
The wood grain looks like old scars.
The stone feels warm under my boots, like an old friend.
The fire crackles, stones warm my boots.
The stone underfoot feels solid, like an old joke waiting.
The fire's crackle matches my steady mind.
The fire flickers, stones warm my boots, I could stay a while.
Crows watch, stone sighs, I keep my steps steady.
The damp log will dry out in the night air.
Log dries, stone cool, I watch.
The fire's crackle matches the steady beat of my heart.
